sources.author: Homer
sources.excerpt: Sing, O goddess, the anger of Achilles son of Peleus, that brought countless ills upon the Achaeans. Many a brave soul did it send hurrying down to Hades.

sources.title: Commentaries on the Gallic War
sources.author: Julius Caesar
sources.excerpt: All Gaul is divided into three parts, one of which the Belgae inhabit, the Aquitani another, those who in their own language are called Celts, in ours Gauls, the third. All these differ from each other in language, customs and laws.
sources.longExcerpt: All Gaul is divided into three parts, one of which the Belgae inhabit, the Aquitani another, those who in their own language are called Celts, in ours Gauls, the third. All these differ from each other in language, customs and laws. This opening of Caesar's military memoirs from 52 BCE became one of the most famous lines in Latin literature, documenting the Roman conquest of Gaul.

sources.title: Germania
sources.author: Tacitus
sources.excerpt: The Germans themselves I should regard as aboriginal, and not mixed at all with other races through immigration or intercourse. For in former times it was not by land but on shipboard that those who sought to emigrate would arrive.
sources.longExcerpt: The Germans themselves I should regard as aboriginal, and not mixed at all with other races through immigration or intercourse. For in former times it was not by land but on shipboard that those who sought to emigrate would arrive. This ethnographic work from 98 CE provides one of the earliest detailed accounts of Germanic tribes, their customs, governance, and way of life beyond the Roman frontier.
